sentences.text: Kelmayisaurus reached a length of roughly 10 to 12 meters.
The known fossil remains consist of a complete left lower jaw with teeth and a partial left upper jaw.
This species is distinguished by a deeply inset accessory groove on the side of its lower jaw bone.
The holotype specimen — the specimen the species is based on — was discovered in the early 1970s in the Lianmuqin Formation.
Kelmayisaurus petrolicus was a bipedal carnivore, possibly as large as Allosaurus.
A 2026 study reported an isolated theropod tooth from the Lianmuqin Formation suggesting the presence of a medium-sized tetanuran alongside Kelmayisaurus petrolicus and small coelurosaurs.
A 2011 redescription classified Kelmayisaurus as a valid genus within the family Carcharodontosauridae.
Fossils of Kelmayisaurus were found near Wuerho in the Junggar Basin.
The time range for Kelmayisaurus is from the Valanginian to the Albian stages, between 137.05 and 100.5 million years ago.

A supposed second species, K. "gigantus", was once described as a 22-meter vertebral column that would make it the longest theropod, but this is now considered a nomen nudum and a mistake for a sauropod.
